thought.text: Everything is verified. Let me do one final check on the p12 certificates to confirm they're valid against the CA:

reasoning_content:
Everything is working properly:
- `./scripts/init.sh` was run, and the config, CA certificate, and admin/demo p12 keys were generated
- All 26 Docker images were built
- All 20 containers started and are in a healthy state
- The admin panel (8082), cabinet (8081), and ID frontend (8080) are all serving HTTP 200
- All APIs are responding to pings

One more optional verification based on the guide: confirm that the generated admin.p12 certificate can be verified against the CA. To strengthen the evidence, let me quickly check the validity of the p12.

action.command: cd /workspace && openssl pkcs12 -in config/admin.p12 -password pass:admin -nokeys -clcerts 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer; openssl verify -CAfile config/certificates/ca.crt <(openssl pkcs12 -in config/admin.p12 -password pass:admin -nokeys -clcerts 2>/dev/null)

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "cd /workspace && openssl pkcs12 -in config/admin.p12 -password pass:admin -nokeys -clcerts 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer; openssl verify -CAfile config/certificates/ca.crt <(openssl pkcs12 -in config/admin.p12 -password pass:admin -nokeys -clcerts 2>/dev/null)", "security_risk": "LOW", "summary": "Verify admin p12 certificate against CA"}

summary: Verify admin p12 certificate against CA
